क्या हिंसक सिनेमा को अपराध की वजह मानना सही है? 🎬

आंध्र प्रदेश में 21 साल के Hemanth ने Class 10 की छात्रा पर इलेक्ट्रिक चैनसो से हमला कर दिया। 😱

इस खौफनाक घटना के बाद सोशल मीडिया पर हिंसक फिल्मों की आलोचना होने लगी।

इस मुद्दे पर सिंगर Amaal Mallik ने X पर अपनी बात रखते हुए हमले की कड़े शब्दों में निंदा की।

Amaal का कहना है कि सिर्फ सिनेमा को जिम्मेदार नहीं ठहराया जा सकता, परवरिश और इंसान की सोच भी मायने रखती है।

उन्होंने बताया कि उन्हें Animal, Kabir Singh, Dhurandhar और KGF जैसी फिल्में काफी पसंद आई हैं।

साथ ही Amaal ने सवाल उठाया कि अगर फिल्मों की आलोचना होती है तो आपत्तिजनक गानों पर बहस क्यों नहीं? 💭

क्या आपको लगता है कि फिल्मों की हिंसा से असली जिंदगी में अपराध बढ़ते हैं? कमेंट्स में बताएं! 👇

The singer also said that even songs shouldn't be spared the scrutiny.
Singer and music composer Amaal Mallik has shared his views on the debate surrounding violent films and their alleged influence on people, following the horrific attack on a Class 10 student in Andhra Pradesh. The incident involved a 21-year-old man named Hemanth, who attacked the student with an electric chainsaw after she rejected his advances.
Following the incident, some people have questioned whether violent films, particularly those made by filmmaker Sandeep Reddy Vanga, encourage such behaviour. Reacting to the discussion, Amaal took to X (formerly Twitter) and said that while films and music can influence young minds, cinema alone cannot be held responsible for an individual's actions.
“I understand why people are concerned. Films and music can influence young people, and some kids copy what they see. Filmmakers should think about how they show violence. But cinema alone cannot be blamed for someone’s actions,” Amaal wrote.
He pointed out that family values, upbringing, the political climate, personal experiences and an individual's way of thinking also play a role. However, he made it clear that none of these factors can ever justify violence. Strongly condemning the Andhra Pradesh incident, he added, “I would never support anyone going into a school, college or any other place to kill someone with a chainsaw. It is horrifying and completely wrong.”
The singer also said that he has enjoyed films like Animal, Kabir Singh, Dhurandhar and KGF, while admitting that he has had issues with certain scenes in some movies. He believes audiences should understand that a film is a story and everything shown on screen need not be imitated in real life.
I understand why people are concerned. Films and music can influence young people, and some kids copy what they see. Filmmakers should think about how they show violence.
But cinema alone cannot be blamed for someone’s actions. Family values, upbringing, the political climate in different states, and the way each person thinks and reacts all matter.
People’s experiences and trauma can affect them too. Everyone has good and bad in them, but none of this excuses violence.
I would never support anyone going into a school, college or any other place to kill someone with a chainsaw. It is horrifying and completely wrong.
The attack in Andhra Pradesh deserves a serious discussion, but we should not assume that one film, song or filmmaker caused it.
I have enjoyed Animal, Kabir Singh, Dhurandhar, KGF and many other films, but I have also had problems with some scenes.
A film is a story, and we should know that we do not have to copy everything we see. Many people work together to make a film. These are recent examples too.
If social media and today’s moral policing had existed in the 70s, 80s and 90s, people would have found plenty to criticise in films from those years as well.
Age ratings should be followed. Parents should not bring infants to films rated -A. We can take the influence of films seriously while also expecting viewers to understand the difference between a story and real life.
If we criticise films, we should be fair and look at songs too. Ban songs like Kar Gayi Chull, Rom Rom Romantic (both my songs), Beedi Jalaile, Pink Lips and Chikni Chameli, Munni Badnaam, why are they celebrated and used on reality shows ??
There are also so many songs and content pieces outside of films, specially rap music available on YouTube and Instagram, especially from the northern belt, about murder, power and aggression. Some songs call women “items” or talk about picking up girls. Parents play these songs around their children and encourage them to dance to them.
It’s an art form, and we all can go right or wrong sometimes, but it’s a bloody imaginative space.
If you are getting so influcned by a film you’re the fool.
